Here we combine machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) with spectral adaptive biasing force enhanced sampling to connect proton transfer and water wire configurations to the underlying free energy landscape. We identify competing influences of long-range electrostatics, system size, temperature, and nuclear quantum motion on the predicted ionization thermodynamics. The free energy surface extends from neutral water to ions separated beyond the solvent-separated ion pair (SSIP). It reveals a transition state in which a proton is shared between the second and third molecules of a three-membered water wire. The contact ion pair is unstable and the SSIP only weakly metastable, so determining pK$_w$ requires sampling longer wires. Long-range electrostatics raise the free energy at ion separations beyond $3\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$. Models with comparable force errors give substantially different free energy profiles in this region. Increasing system size lowers the calculated pK$_w$, while nuclear quantum effects bring it closer to experiment and reproduce the higher pK$_w$ of D$_2$O relative to H$_2$O. These results establish a baseline for interpreting thermodynamic results from MLIP simulations in which charged and polar groups react and diffuse in finite cells. Our analysis also explains how cancellation among competing effects can yield ionization constants close to experiment even when simulations omit several physical contributions.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Optimal asymptotic pure-state conversion under thermal operations
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Quantum thermodynamics seeks to characterize possible state transformations under thermodynamic constraints in microscopic quantum systems. In the fully quantum regime, however, quantum coherence imposes various restrictions on state conversions, and a complete characterization of state convertibility has remained open. Here we resolve this problem for asymptotic conversions between pure states. Specifically, we show that asymptotic convertibility is fully determined by the free-energy and energy-variance ratios. Our result reveals how genuinely quantum effects quantitatively constrain state conversions in quantum thermodynamics.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Perfect Wave Transfer in Nonconformal Tomonaga-Luttinger Liquids
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Perfect wave transfer (PWT) reproduces spatial reflection at a common finite time under a fixed Hamiltonian. We classify this process for open compact bosons and inhomogeneous Tomonaga--Luttinger liquids, distinguishing transfer of oscillator and neutral observables from transfer on the charged field algebra. In the single-charge model, the first two notions coincide. Global transfer additionally requires rephasing of the compact zero mode. For regular reflection-symmetric channels, exact oscillator transfer forces an odd multiple of the optical crossing time and a strictly ordered, parity-compatible spectrum differing from the conformal ladder at only finitely many levels. This spectral condition is also sufficient when the Robin boundary data induced by the physical profile are included. Requiring Neumann conditions after the Liouville transformation instead forces conformality. We construct an explicit, regular one-defect family for every $r>1/2$. Its transfer parameters are precisely the reduced fractions $r=p/q$ with odd numerator and denominator, with shortest transfer time $pL/v_0$. At the delay $3L/v_0$, the $r=3/5$ profile has numerical contrast $K_{\max}/K_{\min}\simeq 12.913$, compared with $81$ for $r=3$. Two independent conservative discretizations show second-order convergence on fixed mode bands. Occupation- and charge-constrained error estimates quantify robustness, while an exact homogeneous-chain calculation explains the $J^{2/3}$ resolved-band scale also observed in the engineered channels. These results provide a spectral design method and finite-device benchmarks for quadratic quantum channels. An interacting microscopic realization remains open.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Deep Learning Theory through the Lens of Statistical Physics: A Topical Review
arXiv_CondMat.summary: The recent success of foundation models and deep learning has far outpaced our theoretical understanding of how large-scale neural networks learn and generalize. Statistical physics provides a natural language for describing such high-dimensional, nonlinear, and strongly coupled systems, offering concepts such as mean-field theory, phase transitions, energy landscapes, and stochastic dynamics. In this topical review, we adopt a statistical-physics way of thinking -- from concepts including phases and criticality, and free-energy viewpoints, to methods such as kernel and Gaussian-process limits, mean-field and dynamical mean-field theories, random-matrix tools, and Fokker-Planck formalisms, and to a mindset emphasizing universality, scaling, and tractable limits with explicit validity regimes. We survey recent progress on understanding modern deep learning through this lens, including mean-field analyses of wide networks, spectral and geometric perspectives on loss landscapes, stochastic-gradient-based training viewed as a dynamical process, and phase-transition analogies that organize phenomena such as overparameterization, generalization, and representation change. Our goal is to synthesize these threads into a coherent framework that clarifies what each approximation explains, when it is expected to hold, and how apparently competing narratives relate or diverge. Together, these perspectives form a unified physical framework that views representation learning as a collective phenomenon in high-dimensional systems, bridging deterministic and stochastic regimes of gradient-based optimization.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Continuum mean-field theory of spatiotemporal pattern formation in a three-state active Potts model
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We investigate the spatiotemporal dynamics of a three-state active Potts model with a cyclic transition bias. Starting from microscopic Glauber-type dynamics, we derive macroscopic continuum field equations through a spatial mean-field approximation. Linear stability and weakly nonlinear analyses reveal that increasing the coupling strength induces a Hopf bifurcation, near which the critical amplitude dynamics is described by the complex Ginzburg--Landau equation. In the spatially homogeneous limit, the system exhibits limit-cycle oscillations and ordered states, with an intermediate regime of bistability bounded by a $\mathbb{Z}_3$-symmetric heteroclinic bifurcation. In two dimensions, the system sustains stable rotating spiral waves. Using perturbation theory based on one-dimensional traveling fronts, we semianalytically predict the curvature-dependent propagation velocity of circular fronts, as well as the rotational angular velocity and pitch of spiral waves. Finally, we compare the continuum model with discrete Monte Carlo simulations to clarify the role of thermal fluctuations and evaluate the validity of the mean-field approximation.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Exploring Variational Regularization of Krylov Subspaces
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Krylov subspace methods efficiently approximate extremal eigenstates and eigenvalues of many-body Hamiltonians, but non-orthogonal bases can suffer from ill-conditioning. This challenge is amplified in quantum computing, where direct state access and thus straightforward orthogonalization are unavailable. We investigate a variational Krylov-like framework that iteratively optimizes a parametrized sequence of states to mimic Lanczos-like couplings while penalizing linear dependencies. Analyzed against exact Krylov and Lanczos on a finite Anderson impurity model, ansatz expressivity strongly influences the performance: Hamiltonian-inspired ans\"atze preserve Krylov-like convergence while improving the conditioning, whereas shallow ans\"atze remain stable but miss low-energy directions.

arXiv_CondMat.title: A State-Variable Theory of Evolving Material Symmetry
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Material architecture can evolve during loading, yet its mechanically expressed symmetry depends on both the structural state and the constitutive coupling. We connect these quantities through one parent-invariant free energy with a symmetric traceless internal tensor $\mathbf Q$. Its stabilizer distinguishes isotropic, uniaxial, and biaxial states, and projected gradient kinetics satisfies the structural dissipation inequality. Parent invariance generally guarantees only symmetry inheritance. For an explicit two-coupling elastic potential, we derive a stiffness-contraction reconstruction of $\mathbf Q$ and prove equality of the structural and tangent rotational symmetries for every nonzero coupling pair. The associated acoustic tensor links residual symmetry to protected transverse degeneracies. For a small uniaxial state, the leading squared-speed gap is $|\gamma_2s|\sin^2\vartheta/(2\rho_0)$; coupling selectivity and residual protection can suppress this term. We also derive a directional acoustic-trace reconstruction and state calibrated and nuisance-aware inverse conditions. Dimensionless structural-field, acoustic, transient finite-element, and synthetic inverse examples illustrate the predictions. The framework connects state evolution, mechanically expressed symmetry, and conditional observability without assigning independent dynamics to a group label.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Optimal performance of driven-dissipative many-body quantum batteries beyond complete nonreciprocity
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Proposals for nonreciprocal quantum batteries identify the point of complete nonreciprocity, where coherent and reservoir-mediated couplings balance, as the operating point for enhanced charging. We show that, for batteries built from interacting qubits, this point is, in general, suboptimal. The optimal design is set by a more intricate interplay between the coherent coupling and the local and collective dissipation rates, of which complete nonreciprocity is only a special case. We consider a many-body battery charged by a driven many-body charger, with each qubit coupled to a local bath and the complete setup immersed in a shared engineered reservoir. For a weakly driven two-qubit setup, we prove the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction to be the optimal coupling, and show that the battery capacity is maximized at a coupling strength fixed by the local and collective dissipation rates, which coincides with complete nonreciprocity only for a specific balance between them. The shared reservoir enhances the capacity for couplings weaker or stronger than both local dissipation rates, and can increase the extractable work even where it reduces the capacity. At strong drive, with the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction between the charger and the battery, the capacity is bounded by $1/2$. For qubits arranged in a star network with a single central battery qubit, these results remain qualitatively unchanged, while the maximum capacity of a battery charged by $N_A$ weakly driven charger qubits saturates with $N_A$ in the presence of the shared reservoir, approaching its limit as $N_A^{-1}$. In contrast, the maximum capacity of $N_B$ qubit batteries charged by a single-qubit charger decays as $N_B^{-2}$.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Increased Crystal Nucleation in the Glassy State of a Polymer/Water Mixture
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Within classical nucleation theory, crystal nucleation requires sufficient supersaturation, but is suppressed at low temperatures due to reduced molecular mobility, leading to a maximum nucleation rate typically above the glass transition temperature $T_g$. Here, we experimentally show that this conventional picture breaks down in a biocompatible polymer poly(2-methoxyethyl acrylate)(PMEA)/water mixture. We find that the number of nuclei increases dramatically below $T_g$, with the effective nucleation rate exhibiting an unusual maximum at approximately $T_g-10$ K. Calorimetric experiments reveal a strong temperature-history dependence of cold crystallization of water in hydrated PMEA, which is explained by the observed nucleation behavior. We propose that the unusual enhancement of nucleation below $T_g$ provides a key mechanism linking high glass-forming ability and cold crystallization upon heating, thereby explaining the striking asymmetry in crystallization behavior between cooling and heating. Our findings suggest that a hidden nucleation-rate maximum below $T_g$ may also underlie cold crystallization in other glass-forming liquids.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Dynamics and pseudospectra around quantum exceptional points
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Exceptional points (EPs) are a hallmark of non-Hermitian physics, giving rise to extreme sensitivity and enhanced dynamic response. Such unique spectral singularities have been extensively studied in classical photonics, both at theoretical and experimental levels, where the relevant observables are evident. That is not necessarily the case in the quantum regime, where this kind of behavior around EPs, to a large extent, remains elusive. In fact, the interplay between dissipation and quantum fluctuations makes the complete Lindbladian evolution quite different from effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian descriptions. In this context, we investigate the signatures of the Liouvillian EPs on spectral and dynamic response by considering properly normalized long-time averages and imbalances. Even though our approach is generic, we focus on two paradigmatic models-a lossy Bose-Hubbard lattice and a dissipative two-spin system, where we investigate the role of quantum jumps and interactions in the Liouvillian spectrum, in terms of complex and structured pseudospectra. Our results demonstrate how non-Hermitian phenomena emerge in realistic quantum lattices, providing a bridge between classical EP physics and experimentally accessible open quantum systems.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Resolving non-neutrality across scales in a hyperdiverse tropical forest
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Different ecological processes operate at different spatial and temporal scales. Macroscopic regularities can therefore be captured by descriptions that ignore microscopic details, even when those details are mechanistically relevant to ecological processes. Here, we develop a framework inspired by statistical mechanics to track interspecific spatial correlations under spatial coarse-graining. To do so we combine random-matrix filtering with a spatially explicit neutral model. Applying this approach to eight censuses of the Barro Colorado Island tropical forest, we observe a continuous crossover from an interacting to an effectively neutral organization. Below a few tens of metres (20--35~m), the empirical correlation spectrum differs from neutral expectations, revealing scale-dependent species-specific structure. Part of this structure can be attributed to environmental heterogeneity. However, residual spatial associations provide candidate signatures of biotic interactions or other unmeasured ecological, non-neutral processes. With increasing spatial coarse-graining, empirical and neutral correlation spectra progressively converge, and above the crossover scale the neutral model provides an accurate description of the measured collective organization. Neutrality thus emerges as an effective description of the collective organization of the forest above a characteristic scale, without implying that species are equivalent at the individual level. Our framework provides an operational way to locate that scale.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Suppression of gel formation by spontaneous fragmentation
arXiv_CondMat.summary: In this work we study the discrete Smoluchowski equation with a multiplicative kernel and an additional term describing the spontaneous shattering of each particle into monomers at a constant rate $\lambda$. We show that the introduction of fragmentation suppresses gelation for $\lambda \ge 4$. We derive analytical expressions for the second moment and the monomer concentration $n_1(t)$. These expressions lead to a recurrence relation allowing the steady-state particle size distribution for $\lambda \ge 4$ to be calculated with machine precision. We validate our analytical and semi-analytical results via numerical simulations using a solver that employs the Fast Fourier Transform for computation of the right-hand side and a second-order Runge-Kutta method with adaptive time steps.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Open Quantum Time Crystals without External Thermodynamic Resources: Go and No-Go Theorems
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Time crystals are phases of matter that spontaneously break time-translation symmetry. They have been ruled out in the ground and Gibbs states of isolated systems with only short-range interactions, yet they have been proposed and observed experimentally in nonequilibrium settings such as Floquet and open systems. However, existing proposals for time crystals in open quantum systems require an external supply of thermodynamic resources, such as work or energetic coherence. Whether coupling to an environment, without any such resource supply, can induce a time crystal absent in the isolated system remains open. Here, we answer this question systematically. We first construct an explicit model and prove that coupling to an environment can activate a time crystal absent in the isolated system, even without such resource supply. We consider Lindblad master equations with (i) time-independent Hamiltonian and jump operators, (ii) time-translation covariance, and (iii) detailed balance---conditions that hold in standard derivations unless thermodynamic resources are supplied externally. Our model satisfies these conditions, and the activation occurs in a stationary state of both the isolated and open systems. We give several implementations of this dynamics with a zero-temperature Gibbs environment, a time-independent, energy-conserving interaction, and only short-range Hamiltonians, one of which exactly reproduces the time-crystalline periodicity. We then prove a no-go theorem: under (i)--(iii), activation can arise only from an environment-induced Hamiltonian term, not from dissipation. Our results show that time crystals can be activated in open systems without external resource supply and identify the physical requirements on the system and environment for this activation through our general no-go theorem.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Synchronization transitions in Kuramoto oscillators with mixed interactions
arXiv_CondMat.summary: The Kuramoto model is a paradigmatic system for emergent synchronization phenomena, and significant efforts have been made to investigate its transition from incoherent to coherent dynamics. However, previous studies have almost exclusively assumed global coupling between the oscillators, even though many real-world systems are organized in specific network structures. Here, we fill this gap by examining finite-size effects in Kuramoto oscillator ensembles on networks with mixed-order interactions. Using numerical simulations, we show how parameters such as the size of the system, the average degree of the nodes and the strength of the interactions alter the behaviour of the transition to synchronization with respect to the known theoretical results that are derived for globally coupled infinite systems.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Modular Hamiltonian and Typicality of Degenerate States
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Free fermions exhibit Eigenstate Typicality (ET) meaning that the reduced density matrix, $\rho$, of a small spatial subsystem of a {\sl single}, typical, excited energy eigenstate is gaussian with a modular hamiltonian, $h \equiv -\log \rho$, asymptotically proportional to the free fermion hamiltonian. In effect, the ET may be thought of as providing an independent route to establishing the Fermi-Dirac (FD) distribution for free fermions. We revisit this argument for fermions belonging to a superposition of degenerate eigenstates. Specifically, we show that the modular hamiltonian corresponding to a superposition of degenerate eigenstates in a 1-d free fermion lattice system is interacting, and therefore the reduced density matrix for the subsystem is not gaussian. Measurements of the single particle distribution of a small subsystem would then exhibit non-thermal deviations from the FD distribution. These features may be traced to a violation of Wick's theorem for the chosen excited state. We develop a perturbation theory for the modular hamiltonian corresponding to a weak mixture of degenerate states and study the modular hamiltonian (exactly) computationally. Finally, we speculate that initial conditions in a realistic fermi system evolving towards equilibrium might be encoded in the interaction terms of the modular hamiltonian and consequent correlations of fermions.
authors: Gregory C. Levine, Goncalo C. Oliveira

arXiv_CondMat.title: Propagating the Hierarchical Equations of Motion using the Multi-Layer Multi-Configurational Time-Dependent Hartree method
arXiv_CondMat.summary: The hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) are a powerful, numerically exact approach for simulating the time evolution of open quantum systems. Recently, several tensor-train- and tensor-network-based approaches have been suggested and realized to extend the range of applicability of the HEOM approach to larger and more realistic systems. In this paper, we build upon the existing twin-space formulation of the HEOM and present a novel approach to propagate the fermionic HEOM efficiently using the multi-configurational time-dependent Hartree method (MCTDH). We benchmark the resulting HEOM+MCTDH method with electron transport calculations for a Holstein-type nanojunction model. Furthermore, we demonstrate the capabilities of the HEOM+MCTDH method by applying it to a more complex vibronic coupling nanojunction model with strong molecule-electrode coupling for which fully quantum simulations have not been feasible previously.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Slow structures, fast degrees of freedom, and the morphology of chess openings
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Chess openings naturally separate into slow and fast degrees of freedom: pawns evolve through irreversible moves, whereas pieces can be rapidly reorganized within the resulting structure. We exploit this separation to construct a quantitative morphology of opening space. From a catalogue of 3810 named variations, 1749 reach a common depth of $N=10$ plies, corresponding to 619 distinct positions and only 435 joint pawn structures. We characterize these positions through observables measuring pawn commitment and spatial organization, blockade and tension, and piece activity and centralization. Their partial independence reveals a multidimensional opening space and in order to explore its structural organization, we construct a network whose nodes are distinct White pawn structures, connected when a single pawn move or capture transforms one into another. Remarkably, 139 of the 149 observed structures belong to a single connected component containing $98\%$ of all positions. This network exhibits a statistically significant modular organization, with eight communities whose representative structures correspond to familiar pawn formations. Rather than forming isolated categories, these formations emerge as distinct regions of a connected structural landscape. Our approach thus complements the traditional opening taxonomy by revealing similarities between differently named openings and providing a quantitative basis for comparing the positions they produce.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Edge dynamics of covariant higher-rank Chern-Simons theory of fractons
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We study the covariant higher-rank Chern-Simons theory of fractons in 2+1 dimensions in the presence of a planar boundary. The differential generator associated with the scalar gauge symmetry singles out a single scalar Ward combination of the functional field equations. Its zeroth and first normal moments give two integrated boundary identities. The zeroth moment yields a traceless rank-two current obeying a fractonic double-divergence conservation law and a higher-rank Kac-Moody algebra. The first moment makes the normal-tangential field $w_i=h_{2i}$ explicit and yields an ordinarily conserved vector current with a standard $U(1)$ Kac-Moody algebra. Functional differentiation also produces a mixed equal-time bulk-boundary commutator between $w_1$ and $h_{11}$: it is non-vanishing at finite normal distance and vanishes in the intrinsic boundary limit. The equal-time commutators of the boundary current with the spatial components of the gauge-invariant field strength vanish, so microcausality is satisfied; when the boundary parameters are such that the two boundary sectors decouple, its retarded response vanishes at all times. Locally, the boundary constraints are solved by $w_i=\partial_i\chi$ and $h_{ij}=\partial_i\partial_j\xi+\eta_{ij}\phi$. When the boundary parameters are such that the two sectors decouple, the induced action is the direct sum of a chiral boson in the $w_i$ sector and a higher-rank sector in which $\phi$ is auxiliary and $\psi=\partial_1\xi$ is the propagating field. The latter has a non-chiral Luttinger description on its positive-energy branch and admits a chiral reduction. The boundary conditions determine the velocity and positivity branch of the $w_i$ mode, while the compatibility analysis in the $h_{ij}$ sector selects the positive-energy branch. On the positive-energy branch the two chiral modes co-propagate with orientation opposite to the sign of $\kappa$.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Arrival-time problem in the quantum information era - observation of a Zeno crossover in monitored arrival-time distributions
arXiv_CondMat.summary: When does a quantum particle arrive at a detector? The temporal distributions of itinerant quantum particles have been debated since the birth of quantum mechanics. Here we study the arrival-time problem in periodically monitored spin chains and quantum circuits. The arrival dynamics exhibits two regimes, the quantum Zeno and the low-monitoring regime, separated by an optimal monitoring period set by the single-particle bandwidth. In support of the theory, on superconducting quantum hardware, we measure arrival-time distributions for single and multiple interacting particles in one- and two-dimensional circuits. The measured distributions resolve both regimes and agree closely with quantum-trajectory theory. The crossover persists in interacting many-particle systems: the optimal monitoring point is preserved while many-body interference reshapes the distributions. Zeno suppression likewise persists in two-dimensional geometry. Together, these results show that the two regimes are a generic feature of monitored propagation rather than a single-particle effect. To our knowledge, our work constitutes the first experimental measurement of arrival-time distributions in a monitored quantum transport setting, addressing one of the longest-standing problems in quantum mechanics.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Gibbsian Entropy for General Wigner Distributions
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We propose a definition of non-equilibrium Gibbsian entropy applicable to general quantum systems, computable from Wigner functions, for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian states. We show that while the Wigner function is a quasi-probability distribution, fundamental results linking observables in repeated observations to the function, such as the law of large numbers, the central limit theorem and, crucially, the relation between the entropy and the cumulant generating function continue to apply. This ideas are the core of the large deviation theory, which allow to formulate a positive-definite definition of entropy based on our ignorance of the underlying state structure after repeated measurements of cumulants. This new definition is a parallel to the Gibbs entropy formulation, but it can also be used in out-of-equilibrium regimes. Some important properties of this entropy are discussed. In addition we derive some information theory quantities such as relative entropy, conditional entropy, mutual information and R\'enyi entropy. We then compare the results with Wehrl entropy for the 1D harmonic oscillator, for pure and mixed states. We conclude the the work discussing potential applications of this new formalism, ranging from quantum correlations beyond entanglement to thermalization in closed quantum systems.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Indirect optical manipulation of the antiferromagnetic order of insulating NiO by ultrafast interfacial energy transfer
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We report the ultrafast, (sub)picosecond reduction of the antiferromagnetic order of the insulating NiO thin film in a Pt/NiO bilayer. This reduction of the antiferromagnetic order is not present in pure NiO thin films after a strong optical excitation. This ultrafast phenomenon is attributed to an ultrafast and highly efficient energy transfer from the optically excited electron system of the Pt layer into the NiO spin system. We propose that this energy transfer is mediated by a stochastic exchange scattering of hot Pt electrons at the Pt/NiO interface.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Numerical investigation of the equilibrium Kauzmann transition in a two-dimensional atomistic glass
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Dense liquids gradually transform into non-equilibrium amorphous solids as they pass through the experimental glass transition. Experimentally, ergodicity is lost because measurements are conducted within a finite time window. More than seventy years ago, Kauzmann posed a fundamental question: If experiments could run indefinitely, would there exist a critical temperature at which an ergodicity-breaking phase transition occurs? Random first-order transitions represent the modern theoretical framework for this idea. However, theoretical calculations in finite dimensions are challenging, whereas experimental and numerical limitations on accessible timescales hinder direct observation of the putative Kauzmann transition. Here, we overcome this longstanding barrier by developing a computational strategy that properly combines three Monte Carlo methods to access the desired equilibrium thermodynamic properties of a two-dimensional atomistic glass-former down to zero temperature across a range of system sizes up to 77 particles. This enables us to directly measure thermodynamic and structural observables that provide unambiguous evidence that the system undergoes a finite-size version of the Kauzmann transition at a temperature that is much lower than other energy scales and decreases rapidly with system size, thus suggesting the existence of a zero-temperature Kauzmann transition for two-dimensional glasses. The transition is towards an ideal glass state characterized by a complex energy landscape and a hierarchical organization of low-lying states.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Dual topology and edge-reconstruction in $\alpha$-Sn
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We formulate the tight-binding model for cubic $\alpha$-Sn based on the DFT calculations. In the model, we incorporate a variable bond angle, which allows us to simulate the effect of the in-plane strain. In the bulk, we demonstrate the presence of the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological invariant and a non-zero mirror Chern number, making $\alpha$-Sn one of the rare cases where dual topology can be observed. We calculate the topological phase diagram of multi-layer $\alpha$-Sn as a function of strain and number of layers. We find that a non-trivial quantum spin Hall state appears only for compressive strain above five layers of thickness. Quite surprisingly, both in the trivial and non-trivial phases, we find a plethora of edge-states with energies inside the bulk gap of the system. Some of these states are localized at the side surfaces of the slab and some of them prefer top/bottom surfaces. We find that they can be adiabatically connected to topological states in the chiral limit, where the model supports multiple one-dimensional winding numbers that take different values in different directions in the Brillouin zone. Finally, around high-symmetry points their presence can also be explained by the mirror Chern number and Wilson-loop invariants

arXiv_CondMat.title: Spin-density wave of ferrimagnetic building blocks masking the ferromagnetic quantum-critical point in NbFe2
arXiv_CondMat.summary: In the metallic magnet NbFe2, the low temperature threshold of ferromagnetism can be investigated by varying the Fe concentration within a narrow homogeneity range. NbFe2 is one of a number of compounds where modulated order is found to mask the ferromagnetic quantum critical point. However, here we report the rare case where the masking modulated magnetic order has been fully refined. Spherical neutron polarimetry and high-intensity single-crystal neutron diffraction reveal the first case of a longitudinal spin-density wave masking the ferromagnetic quantum critical point. The spin-density wave is characterised by a large-wavelength incommensurate modulation of its low average moment. It is formed from ferrimagnetic building blocks with antiparallel ferromagnetic sheets. The existence of ferromagnetic sheets and cancellation of the magnetisation only over mesoscopic length scales show local similarity between the spin-density wave and the ferromagnetic parent phase and indicate the spin-density wave's unconventional nature as emerging from underlying ferromagnetic quantum criticality.
authors: F. M. Grosche, P. G. Niklowitz

arXiv_CondMat.title: AtomMOF: All-Atom Flow Matching for MOF-Adsorbate Structure Prediction
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising materials for applications such as direct air capture, where performance depends on how adsorbates bind within the framework. Accurately predicting MOF-adsorbate configurations is therefore important for screening candidate materials. However, traditional approaches are computationally expensive and require a known host structure, while existing generative models rely on rigid-body assumptions and do not explicitly model adsorbates. We introduce AtomMOF, a scalable all-atom flow-matching model that jointly predicts MOF-adsorbate structures from discrete building blocks and adsorbates. Built on a Diffusion Transformer with a building block-based pairwise attention bias, AtomMOF operates in an unconstrained all-atom space and exhibits clear scaling behavior. To improve the structural validity of flexible all-atom models, we also propose Feynman-Kac (FK) steering with machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs). On the BW dataset, AtomMOF achieves a 85.61% relative increase in match rate and a 34.32% relative reduction in RMSD compared with prior work. MLIP-guided steering further improves validity by 28.7% and reduces formation energy error by 86.5%. On ODAC25, AtomMOF generates adsorption configurations faster than GCMC and, when combined with MLIP relaxation, identifies lower-energy configurations than those in the reference dataset.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Surface-Dominated Anomalous Hall Effect in Altermagnetic MnTe Films
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Altermagnets have recently emerged as a new class of magnetic materials that combine compensated magnetic order with spin-split electronic band structures. In this work, we employ molecular beam epitaxy to grow MnTe thin films with controlled thickness on InP(111)A substrates. Using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, we observe a large spin splitting of $\approx 230$ meV for bulk bands well below the Fermi level and identify surface states that cross the Fermi level. Electrical transport measurements show that a robust anomalous Hall (AH) effect persists down to 2 K and an AH sign reversal occurs near 175 K. By systematically tuning film thickness, growth conditions, and interfacial structure, we demonstrate that the AH response in MnTe films originates from surface states rather than bulk bands. Our first-principles calculations reveal that this surface-dominated AH effect is imprinted by the bulk altermagnetic order and remains unchanged for terminations with opposite Mn magnetic orientations. Our results establish a unique surface transport probe of bulk altermagnetism, demonstrate interface engineering as an effective route to generate and control the AH effect in altermagnets, and provide a unified understanding of the AH response in altermagnetic MnTe films.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Computational discovery of cathode materials for rechargeable aqueous zinc-ion batteries
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Rechargeable aqueous zinc-ion batteries (RAZIBs) attract major interest for deployment in grid-scale energy storage due to higher safety and lower cost when compared to lithium-ion batteries. However, currently studied cathode materials suffer from capacity fade when cycling at rates appropriate for grid-scale applications ($<$ C/2). To address the present limitation on cathode material availability, more than 2000 previously synthesized oxides, chalcogenides, Prussian blue analogues, and polyanion materials were computationally screened for the discovery of highly stable RAZIB cathode materials. The structural, electrochemical, and chemical properties of the materials were respectively evaluated through an investigation of the available Zn$^{2+}$ percolation paths, the stability of the material in aqueous media under RAZIB operation conditions, and the attained transition metal oxidation state during cycling. The transition metal oxidation state and intercalating ion coordination environment were determined to govern the magnitude of the calculated Zn$^{2+}$ intercalation potential, with this finding guiding the development of batteries with high operating voltages. Additionally, the bonding character of Fe-O bonds was contrasted between olivine-FePO$_4$ and $\alpha$-FePO$_4$. The latter was successfully synthesized but was found to be electrochemically inactive as a cathode for RAZIBs. Finally, three previously synthesized materials, but unexplored as cathodes for RAZIBs (CaFe$_5$P$_5$O$_{22}$, RbV(PO$_4$)$_2$, and Mo$_2$P$_2$O$_{11}$), were identified to have high Zn$^{2+}$ intercalation potential, electrochemical stability, theoretical gravimetric capacity, and energy density, and are proposed here for further experimental testing. Overall, the materials identified in this study present a guide for the experimental development of stable next-generation cathode materials for RAZIBs.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Embedding stochastic dynamics in latent manifolds of recurrent neural networks
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) provide a theoretical framework for understanding computation in biological neural circuits through their ability to support rich time-dependent behaviour. Whilst high-dimensional by construction, they can be used to encode low-dimensional dynamical systems, for example by restricting to low-rank connectivity, hence mirroring the emergence of latent neural manifolds found in empirical neural data. Here, we exploit a relationship between RNNs and a class of universal approximators to train networks that can represent arbitrary, nonlinear stochastic differential equations (SDEs), with given drift and diffusion coefficients, within a low-dimensional latent subspace. We show that RNNs can faithfully embed the drift and diffusion of a given SDE, including nonlinear and nonequilibrium dynamics such as chaotic attractors. We apply this approach by constructing RNN realisations of stochastic systems that transiently explore various attractors through both input-driven switching and autonomous transitions driven by nonequilibrium currents, which we interpret as models of associative and sequential (episodic) memory. To elucidate how these dynamics are encoded in the network, we introduce decompositions of the RNN based on its asymmetric connectivity and its time-irreversibility. Our results show that neural populations can implement a broad class of stochastic dynamics within low-dimensional manifolds, unifying ideas from the dynamics of neural computation, the theory of neural manifolds, associative memory, and nonequilibrium statistical mechanics.

arXiv_CondMat.title: On deforming and breaking integrability
arXiv_CondMat.summary: In this paper we study nearest-neighbour deformations of integrable models. After expanding in the deformation parameter, we identify four possible types of deformations. First there are deformations that simply break or preserve integrability. Then we find two different subtle cases. The first case is where the deformation is only integrable if all orders of the deformation parameter are taken into account. An example of these are the long-range deformations that appear in holographic models. The second case is when the deformation is perturbatively integrable to some order in the deformation parameter but can not be extended to an integrable model. In this paper we work this out for the XXZ spin chain and discuss the level statistics of each of these cases. We find numerical evidence that the onset of chaos occurs differently in each of these models. For the perturbatively integrable models, we find that the deformation strength at which chaos appears demonstrates a volume-scaling intermediate between strong and weak integrability breaking models.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Tackling the Sign Problem in the Doped Hubbard Model with Normalizing Flows
arXiv_CondMat.summary: The Hubbard model at finite chemical potential is a cornerstone for understanding doped correlated systems, but simulations are severely limited by the sign problem. In the auxiliary-field formulation, the spin basis mitigates the sign problem, yet severe ergodicity issues have limited its use. We extend recent advances with normalizing flows at half-filling to finite chemical potential by introducing an annealing scheme enabling ergodic sampling. Compared to state-of-the-art hybrid Monte Carlo in the charge basis, our approach accurately reproduces exact diagonalization results while reducing statistical uncertainties by an order of magnitude, opening a new path for simulations of doped correlated systems.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Universal Pareto fronts and trade-off relations in multi-objective optimization of thermal machines
arXiv_CondMat.summary: The performance of thermal machines is characterized with several, often competing quantities, such as power, efficiency, energy waste, and resilience to environmental noise. We employ multi-objective optimization to find the best thermal machines operating in the irreversible linear-response regime. We derive exact analytical parameterizations for the optimal (Pareto) fronts associated with mean extracted power, efficiency, entropy production and the amplitude of power fluctuations. These optimal fronts set the quantitative fundamental limits for the performance of linear-response machines, which are achieved under tight coupling conditions (endoreversible machines). The geometry of the fronts is universal: two-, three-, and four-objective trade-offs follow analytical formulae that do not depend on the value of any physical parameter of the machine. Furthermore, we test our results with existing experimental data from different physical systems operating also beyond the linear regime, ranging from atomic to macroscopic scales, and including single-atom engines, colloidal systems, macroscopic engines and power plants.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Electric toroidal octupolar symmetry in pyrite FeS$_2$ probed by Raman optical activity
arXiv_CondMat.summary: In crystals with degenerate phonons, Raman optical activity (ROA), the difference in Raman scattering intensity between circular polarization channels, can arise when the scattering distinguishes components carrying opposite crystal angular momenta. In crystals it has long been associated with structural chirality and more recently with ferroaxial order, which are the electric toroidal multipoles of rank zero and rank one, but whether it can probe higher ranks has remained unknown. Here we report ROA in pyrite FeS$_2$, a centrosymmetric and nonmagnetic crystal whose $T_h$ symmetry forbids the electric toroidal multipoles of ranks zero, one, and two, so that the lowest-rank one it admits is the octupole of rank three. Using circularly polarized Raman scattering in a backscattering geometry, we observe a pronounced circular intensity difference exclusively for the doubly degenerate $E_g$ phonon, reaching about 85% of the mean intensity at an excitation wavelength of 633 nm. The difference reverses sign reproducibly between neighboring {111} facets and is strongly suppressed on {001}. Group theory shows that this difference transforms as the antisymmetric part of the self-product of the mode representation, which contains the octupolar $A_{2g}$ representation for the $E_g$ doublet but not for the $T_g$ triplets and that it must vanish for propagation along $\langle 001 \rangle$. First-principles resonant Raman calculations, evaluated at the three experimental photon energies within the electric-dipole approximation, reproduce the $E_g$ selectivity and the reversal of sign with excitation energy. These results extend ROA from rank-one to rank-three axial multipolar symmetry and establish it as a symmetry-selective, facet-resolved optical probe of symmetries that produce neither macroscopic polarization nor magnetization.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Feedback percolation on complex networks
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Traditional percolation theory assumes static microscopic rules, limiting its ability to describe real-world complex systems where macroscopic order actively regulates local interactions. Here, we introduce feedback percolation, an unified framework that dynamically couples the microscopic activation probability to the macroscopic size of the giant component. We show that this simple feedback mechanism produces a rich variety of behaviors both analytically and numerically. Depending on the feedback functions, the system exhibits explosive discontinuous jumps, hybrid transitions, limit-cycle oscillations, and routes to chaos, absent in classical percolation. Our findings establish that macroscopic feedback provides a unifying physical mechanism for phenomena ranging from self-regulating oscillations to systemic infrastructure collapse.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Predicting accurate solid-state thermodynamics is easier than you think
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Materials underpin modern technologies, from energy harvesting, storage, and conversion to information and communication technologies. Their functionality is often governed by the interplay between competing phases, and thermodynamic behavior shapes microscopic properties and ultimately determines technological performance; for instance, the light absorption of inorganic metal-halide perovskites in solar cells. Accurately predicting crystal thermodynamics, however, remains a major challenge for computational approaches because strong anharmonic effects require extensive sampling of the potential energy surface. Here, we present an on-the-fly Bayesian framework, combined with the stochastic self-consistent harmonic approximation, for learning first-principles potentials. This approach enables the prediction of thermodynamic properties over a broad temperature range with first-principles accuracy while requiring training on only a few atomic configurations. A relevant finding is that the majority of the required structures are obtained from a single inexpensive dataset generation step, demonstrating that the relevant physics for accurately predicting solid-state thermodynamics is encoded in a few physically meaningful configurations. We investigate the thermodynamic and dynamical properties of Li$_2$O, $\alpha$--CsPbI$_3$, and $\delta$--CsPbI$_3$, requiring only 44, 256, and 50 total-energy calculations, respectively. Notably, we show that this framework accurately captures the extreme thermal expansion of \ce{Li2O}, and the phase diagram of CsPbI$_3$ with a predicted transition temperature within 20 K of experiment. More broadly, the method presented opens an interesting route toward accelerated materials engineering under realistic conditions for a wide range of technologically relevant applications, including batteries, photovoltaics, and memristors.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Accurate description of the electronic states of the V$_{\text{B}}^-$ center in hBN by wavefunction theory
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Ensembles of negatively charged boron vacancy (V$_{\text{B}}^-$) centers in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) have emerged as a two-dimensional spin qubit system interfaced with optics to advance nanoscale quantum sensing. However, a comprehensive description of its optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) signal remains challenging due to the strongly correlated nature of the excited electronic states involved in its optical cycle. In this work, we model the energetics, structural relaxation, and transition rates of the V$_{\text{B}}^-$ center using a high-level wave-function-based electron correlation method (CASSCF-NEVPT2). We provide a thorough analysis of the excited state fine structure and pseudo Jahn-Teller effects, singlet-triplet quasi-degeneracies, photoluminescence parameters, intersystem crossing pathways, and stress-dependence of the fine structure and decay parameters. Our findings not only clarify the fundamental behavior of the V$_{\text{B}}^-$ center in hBN but also establish the theoretical foundation for advancing the V$_{\text{B}}^-$ center's readout for integrated 2D quantum sensors.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Strain-Dependent Ionic Transport in Li3YCl6 Solid Electrolytes
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Solid-state batteries require electrolytes that sustain high ionic conductivity under the mechanical environment of a functioning cell. Lattice strain, arising from stack pressure, lattice mismatch at interfaces, and more importantly electrochemical cycling, can either enhance or suppress Li$^+$ transport in solid electrolytes, yet how it couples to the underlying diffusion mechanism in Li3YCl6 remains poorly understood. Using Li3YCl6 halide superionic conductor, we address this with large-scale molecular dynamics simulations driven by an Atomic Cluster Expansion (ACE) machine learning interatomic potential trained on first-principles data. The ACE model faithfully reproduces experimental and ab initio structural, mechanical, and transport properties of Li3YCl6. Extending the simulations to high temperature reveals a crossover from predominantly one-dimensional hopping at low temperature toward diffusion through a connected three-dimensional pathway network at high temperature. Strain substantially modulates diffusivity: tensile strain enhances it while compressive strain suppresses it. Free-breakpoint model selection resolves two Arrhenius regimes for most strain states, and the fitted $T_c$ varies nonmonotonically with strain. Strain modifies the effective activation energies and the accessibility of diffusion pathways in a temperature-dependent manner. These results quantify the strain sensitivity of ionic conductivity and diffusion pathways in Li3YCl6 solid-state electrolytes.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Effective increase of a superconducting critical temperature due to a configurational entropy of impurities
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We show theoretically that a superconducting critical temperature can be effectively increased in a fine-grained superconductor, where impurities migrate along the grain boundaries. The distribution of impurities affects the spatial profile of the BCS condensate. Thus, BCS condensate acquires entropy equal to the configurational entropy of impurities. In order to employ this entropy into the superconducting phase dynamics, we suggest to use a quasiparticle trap that removes quasiparticle excitations from the superconductor. This makes the concentration of Cooper pairs a dynamic variable of the entropy, and thus influences the Ginzburg-Landau functional of the superconductor effectively reducing the first expansion coefficient or, in other words, increasing the critical temperature.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Phonon-driven nodal surface superconductivity of Fermi arcs
arXiv_CondMat.summary: According to recent observations, the topological surface states of Weyl semimetals may develop a superconducting gap, while bulk superconductivity remains absent. What drives the formation of this novel superconducting state is an open question. Here, we show that this phenomenon can arise from the interaction of Fermi arc electrons with both surface and bulk phonons in time-reversal-invariant Weyl semimetals. We identify two competing pairing channels, intra-arc and inter-arc, whose relative strength is governed by the efficiency of Coulomb screening at the surface. The combined effect of the Fermi arcs being disconnected and the weak screening of the Coulomb repulsion at the system's surface causes nodes to appear in the superconducting gap, as observed recently by photoelectron spectroscopy experiments on PtBi2. This suggests manipulation of the Coulomb screening, e.g. by a surface layer coating, as a pathway to engineer the critical temperature, as well as size and symmetry of the surface superconducting gap.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Descriptor Non-Uniqueness in Symbolic Regression: Conditional Bayesian Analysis of SISSO Supports
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Compact analytical descriptors connect materials properties with interpretable combinations of physical and chemical variables, yet different expressions can capture similar trends in small datasets. We present a conditional Bayesian framework for quantifying competition among symbolic descriptors retained by the Sure Independence Screening and Sparsifying Operator (SISSO) method. Exact enumeration of fixed-size supports within the screened feature union yields posterior support probabilities, feature inclusion probabilities, and Bayesian-model-averaged predictions. Applied to magnetic moments of 88 full-Heusler alloys, the framework reveals substantial descriptor non-uniqueness even when the maximum-a-posteriori support coincides with deterministic SISSO. At both two and three descriptor dimensions, eight supports are required to accumulate 95\% posterior probability. Two prominent two-dimensional coordinates exhibit a Pearson correlation of 0.943 despite their distinct algebraic forms. Five-fold validation with screening repeated within each training fold shows higher prediction errors for Bayesian model averaging and undercoverage of nominal predictive intervals, separating descriptor competition from predictive performance. By making statistically competitive expressions explicit, the framework complements deterministic symbolic regression and provides a probabilistic basis for interpreting composition-property relationships in materials modeling.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Thermodynamic Approach to Momentum Transport in Dense Fluids
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We present a new framework for extending Chapman-Enskog theory beyond the hard-sphere fluid model. Rather than relying on effective hard sphere diameters, the approach makes use of on an exchange function which can be related to the thermodynamic properties of the system. We show that two existing extensions, including modified Enskog theory (MET), fit into this new framework. Based on our approach, we propose an alternative to MET that takes into account the potential interaction energy associated with the inter-particle interactions in the fluid. The proposed expression is applied to predicting the shear viscosity of several different simulated fluid models across a wide set of densities $0.05 \leq \rho^* \leq 0.8$ and temperatures $1.5 \leq T^* \leq 4.0$ in Lennard-Jones units. The fluid models considered include both the Weeks-Chandler-Anderson (WCA) fluid and the Lennard-Jones (LJ) fluid. At low and intermediate density, here taken to be $\rho^* \leq 0.3$, we report mean relative prediction errors between $2\%$ and $4\%$ for both these. Across all densities considered, the largest mean relative errors reported are $4.4\%$ and $8.1\%$ for the WCA fluid and LJ fluid respectively. We also investigate other interaction models, including a diatomic molecular model, in order to better understand the limitations of our approach.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Second-order dc conductivity in the velocity-gauge Keldysh formalism: gauge-invariant decomposition into nonlinear Drude, Berry-curvature-dipole, and quantum-metric responses
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We derive a gauge-invariant clean-limit decomposition of the second-order dc nonlinear conductivity in multiband tight-binding systems within the velocity-gauge Keldysh Green's function formalism. In the constant-relaxation-time approximation, the dc response separates into four contributions with distinct lifetime $\tau$ scalings and physical origins: the nonlinear Drude term $\sigma^{\mathrm{ND}}_{ijk}\propto\tau^{2}$, the Berry-curvature-dipole term $\sigma^{\mathrm{BCD}}_{ijk}\propto\tau$, the intraband quantum-metric-dipole term $\sigma^{\mathrm{intra\text{-}QMD}}_{ijk}\propto\tau^{0}$, and the interband quantum-metric-dipole term $\sigma^{\mathrm{inter\text{-}QMD}}_{ijk}\propto\tau^{0}$. The intraband term is a Fermi-surface dipole of the ordinary band quantum metric, while the interband term is written, in the present representation, as a Fermi-sea-type response involving a band-normalized quantum metric. Working entirely within the velocity-gauge Keldysh--Kubo framework, we show that all connection-dependent commutator terms generated in the band-basis expansion cancel exactly between the covariant-quantum-connection sector $\sigma^{\mathcal{C}}_{ijk}$ and the three-Berry-connection sector $\sigma^{\mathcal{T}}_{ijk}$, making the role of the Peierls contact velocity vertices $V_{ij}$ and $V_{ijk}$ explicit; a complementary projector-based derivation appears in Ulrich et al., Phys. Rev. B 113, L201107 (2026), and our Fermi-surface dc-limit expression agrees with that reference after accounting for index and convention differences. As a diagnostic illustration, we introduce a real two-band model in which the Berry curvature and hence the BCD response vanish identically while the intraband quantum-metric dipole remains finite, establishing a practical route to quantum-metric dc responses not reducible to the Berry-curvature-dipole mechanism.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Broadband molecular dynamics simulation of confined Brownian motion
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Molecular dynamics with an explicit solvent resolves the hydrodynamic response of a Brownian colloid in bulk and near a rigid wall over acoustic, inertial, and diffusive time scales. Bulk spectra establish a continuum reference and reveal departures associated with discrete-solvent dynamics. Under confinement, thermal spectra provide a measurement of the space-dependent added mass, while velocity autocorrelations determine space-dependent, anisotropic hydrodynamic memory and diffusion. All together, these measurements connect the enhanced added mass and reduced mobility near a wall, and probe the discrete-continuum crossover.

arXiv_CondMat.title: A modified Moss rule highlights underexplored classes of high refractive index materials
arXiv_CondMat.summary: High refractive index dielectrics are central to photonic applications, yet the empirical Moss rule imposes a fundamental trade-off between refractive index and optical transparency. We introduce a modified Moss rule anchored to the optical absorption edge rather than the fundamental bandgap, capturing materials where various physical mechanisms suppress absorption well above the electronic gap. Screening the Materials Project database with this metric reveals recurring chemical compositions and structural prototypes in the materials with the most promising refractive index/transparency trade-offs. These materials include chalcopyrites, Zintl pnictides, and early transition metal multi-anion chalconitrides and oxichalcogenide compounds. Hybrid density functional theory calculations reveal that the chalconitride (Hf,Zr)2(S,Se)N2 family can achieve a combination of ultra-high refractive indices, low effective masses and transparency windows extending into the UV, potentially surpassing state-of-the-art TiO2. Our results establish (Hf,Zr)2(S,Se)N2 compounds as a unique and largely unexplored material family for next-generation photonic applications.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Tunable Signal Penetration and Response Plateaus in Bistable Mechanical Media
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Dynamic processing of mechanical signals is crucial for soft robotics and mechanosensing, yet classical viscoelastic materials lack intrinsic tunability and quantitative design rules. We show that internal bistability provides a simple but powerful mechanism to tailor response and signal attenuation in mechanical (meta)materials. In our model, bistable elements switch discretely with an intrinsic timescale between states that differ in potential energy $\epsilon$, equilibrium length $\Delta l$, and spring constant $\Delta k$. We combine Brownian dynamics simulations with discrete Poisson switching at rate $\nu$ and a nonlinear continuum (field) theory for the macroscopic strain relaxation. The model yields closed-form solutions for the linear response and the spatial penetration depth, revealing two complementary phenomena: a universal screening mechanism (akin to the electrostatic `skin effect') that strongly reduces signal penetration when the driving frequency exceeds the internal relaxation rate, and a frequency-insensitive response plateau arising from timescale separation. The attenuation strength, expressed by a screening length, is controlled primarily by the conformational length change $\Delta l$, while the attenuation regime and plateau position are tuneable via $\nu$. A parameter study exposes a fundamental design trade-off: larger $\Delta l$ strengthen dissipation but also raise the elastic energy barrier for state transitions, eventually causing state-locking where damping vanishes. Optimal attenuation thus emerges from a compromise between pronounced bistability and a surmountable barrier. Owing to its analytical tractability and generic formulation, our framework yields explicit design rules applicable to systems from biopolymers to synthetic catch bonds and metamaterials, enabling the design of soft materials with frequency-selective mechanical response.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Quantum-classical crossover in finite spin-1/2 rings with Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya interaction
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We study finite spin-$\tfrac12$ rings with nearest-neighbor Heisenberg exchange, Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya interaction, and an external magnetic field. We introduce a phenomenological interpolation parameter between the fully quantum Hamiltonian and a state-dependent mean-field description. Using dissipative Gisin-Schr\"odinger dynamics, we analyze the resulting quantum-classical crossover through local magnetization, connected spin correlations, single-site entropy, and the saturation field of the fully polarized state.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Stoner transitions beyond mean-field in two-dimensional electronic systems: a diagrammatic Monte Carlo study
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Stoner instabilities for fermions with repulsive interaction have been well studied within the mean-field (ladder) approximation. In this study, we consider two-dimensional electronic systems with one or two valleys and discuss a Stoner transition beyond the ladder approximation. At weak coupling, the corrections to the ladder approximation come predominantly from the renormalization of the particle-hole vertex in the particle-particle channel, and the lowest-order corrections are logarithmically singular in the low-density limit. To investigate the problem beyond the lowest order, we apply the diagrammatic Monte Carlo algorithm and treat ladder and non-ladder renormalizations on equal footing. We find that in a one-valley system, a Stoner transition to a ferromagnetism occurs at low density only if there is a cutoff on the momentum transfer carried by the interaction. In a two-valley system, the restriction is less severe. Here we find either a direct Stoner transition into a spin- and valley-polarized state, or a set of two Stoner transitions via an intermediate valley-polarized state. The pathway is controlled by the anisotropy of the fermionic dispersion.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Angular momentum splitter effect of $d$-wave axial phonons in orbital altermagnets
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We theoretically demonstrate that axial phonons, lattice vibration quanta carrying finite angular momentum, can host a $d$-wave angular momentum texture in orbital altermagnets in the absence of spin-orbit coupling. We consider a minimal electronic tight-binding model with $d$-wave loop-current order that breaks time-reversal symmetry. Within the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, we incorporate electron-phonon coupling via the molecular Berry curvature and show that the underlying $d$-wave orbital magnetic moment texture of the electronic state is transferred to the phonons without requiring the relativistic spin-orbit coupling. Our results expand the range of platforms available for engineering axial phonons and point to functionality unique to $d$-wave textures, including angular-momentum Seebeck and splitter effects, corresponding to longitudinal and transverse angular-momentum currents driven by a temperature gradient.

arXiv_CondMat.title: A numerical study to analyze the interplay of Weissenberg number and viscosity ratio in a log-strain tensorial model for viscoelastic fluids
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We present a computational study aimed at exploring the different and independent roles of the Weissenberg number and of the ratio between the polymeric and solvent viscosity contributions in a viscoelastic fluid model. The tensorial model under investigation, recently proposed, is based on a logarithmic relation between the elastic (or recoverable) strain and the elastic stress. In this model, the elastic strain plays the role of a conformation tensor and its evolution equation inherently preserves its determinant and positive definiteness. These properties are also enforced in the computational method employed in the study. A finite-difference discretization in time is combined with a stabilized mixed finite element formulation based on the Variational Multiscale method for the spatial discretization and with a generalized Lie derivative approach for the advection terms. The behavior of the model is analyzed in paradigmatic pressure-driven flows and we find that the value of the viscosity ratio is crucial in determining to which extent non-Newtonian flow profiles are observed upon increasing the Weissenberg number. By comparing the solutions of the log-strain tensorial model with those of a suitable Generalized Newtonian Fluid model, we show that flow-type dependence and memory play a significant role even in the simple planar flow past a cylinder.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Multiscale Quasiparticle Electronic Structure and Excitonic Properties of CdSe Nanoclusters
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Quantum confinement in stoichiometric $\mathrm{Cd}_n\mathrm{Se}_n$ nanoclusters dramatically attenuates electronic screening, driving a delicate, size-dependent competition between quasiparticle self-energy corrections ($\Delta_{\mathrm{QP}}$) and exciton binding energies ($E_b$). Here, we present a $GW$/BSE study across a representative size series ($n = 3, 6, 13, 33$) and leverage it to validate a scalable atomistic tight-binding (TB) framework derived from first principles. Our results demonstrate that 1-2 eV spectral blueshifts previously reported in the literature arise from single-particle $GW$ convergence artifacts rather than deficiencies in the electron--hole kernels. We show that the near-perfect cancellation between $\Delta_{\mathrm{QP}}$ and $E_b$ breaks down as cluster volume increases, driven by the rapid onset of dielectric screening attenuating $E_b$ faster than $\Delta_{\mathrm{QP}}$ and leading to a pronounced divergence from mean-field predictions. Spatial inverse participation ratio analysis of the electronic structure reveals that optical suppression of fundamental pre-peaks stems from a severe spatial mismatch between localized valence orbitals and delocalized conduction states. Finally, we demonstrate that the confinement-induced scaling of the quasiparticle gap and the optical onset is accurately reproduced by a scissor-corrected, DFT-parameterized TB model. As such, this work provides a quantitative multiscale roadmap for embedding effective many-body effects kernels into computationally efficient models, enabling reliable optical predictions for realistic semiconducting nanostructures containing up to thousands of atoms.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Exact quantum geometry from sublattice symmetry: Closed-form solution of the quarter-flux Harper-Hofstadter model
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Quantum geometry has emerged as a guiding principle across atomic and condensed-matter physics, shaping the topological responses of Bloch bands and the stability of the correlated phases they host. Sublattice symmetry, though common among bipartite lattice models, has not yet been exploited to obtain closed-form quantum geometry in multiband systems. For this purpose, we derive a general expression for the QGT of sublattice-symmetric systems in terms of contributions from the individual sublattice sectors, and show that this symmetry renders the Bloch Hamiltonian of a paradigmatic four-band model, the quarter-flux Harper-Hofstadter model, anti-block-diagonal, analytically yielding the spectrum, eigenstates, and full quantum geometric tensor (QGT), including the Berry curvature and quantum metric, for all four bands. The model, describing charged particles on a two-dimensional square lattice subjected to a uniform magnetic field, has recently been realized experimentally with ultracold atoms, photons, and superconducting circuits. Finally, we evaluate fractional-Chern-insulator stability criteria analytically and quantify the lowest band of the quarter-flux Harper-Hofstadter model to be a nearly ideal Chern band. Our approach opens a route for studying also the quantum geometry of other sublattice-symmetric multiband systems.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Narrow-Sense Type-III Dirac Cones and Additional Flat Lines on a Honeycomb Lattice with Anisotropic Next-Nearest-Neighbor Hoppings
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Critically tilted Dirac cones have attracted considerable attention because of their unconventional electronic properties in two-dimensional massless Dirac-fermion systems. Among them, the narrow-sense type-III Dirac cone is characterized by a flat dispersion along the direction connecting the two Dirac points. Using a tight-binding model on a single-orbital honeycomb lattice, we demonstrate that narrow-sense type-III Dirac cones can be realized by tuning anisotropic next-nearest-neighbor hoppings. Type-I and type-II Dirac cones emerge on either side of the critical point, enabling a systematic investigation of the electronic properties across the type-I, narrow-sense type-III, and type-II regimes. We further find that the present model exhibits additional flat lines in momentum space whose energy coincides with the Dirac-point energy at the narrow-sense type-III critical point. These flat lines lead to a pronounced enhancement of the density of states above the Fermi energy and, consequently, the electronic specific heat is substantially enhanced compared with that expected for an ideal narrow-sense type-III Dirac cone. Our results show that the honeycomb lattice with anisotropic next-nearest-neighbor hoppings provides a simple platform for exploring unconventional thermodynamic properties arising from the energy coincidence of narrow-sense type-III Dirac cones and additional flat lines at the Fermi energy.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Liquid-liquid phase transitions in dipolar liquids. Insights into Supercooled Water
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Dipolar liquids combine two coupled degrees of freedom, translational and dipolar. Intriguingly, these two sectors can reside in distinct thermodynamic states, with the state of one sector possibly favouring a specific state of the other. The onset of ferroelectric order in dipolar liquids is an example of this mutual stabilization. Since this coupling is often encoded in interaction potentials, projecting out one sector to derive an effective interaction for the other can uncover the microscopic mechanism underlying this phenomenon. A coarse-grained theory, solved in the large-dimensional limit, in which the distance between nearest-neighbour particles depends on their dipolar interaction through a density-dependent mechanical compliance shows that a ferroelectric transition can trigger a liquid-liquid transition. It also predicts a first-order liquid-liquid transition within the paraelectric phase that, in turn, can promote ferroelectric ordering. The anisotropic dipolar-dependent soft-core interaction is shown to lead to an effective Jagla-like isotropic two-length-scale interaction, known to support liquid-liquid phase transitions. Here, however, the two-length-scale pattern depends on density and dipolar configuration, and is therefore sensitive to dipolar order. Analysis of supercooled TIP4P/Ice water molecular dynamics simulations shows that first-coordination-shell features of the pair correlation functions are sensitive to dipolar interaction, supporting the foundations of the coarse-grained theory. Comparison of low- and high-density liquid water reveals enhanced spatial anisotropy of the first coordination shell in the low-density liquid, associated, within the theory, with increased effective excluded volume, showing that the liquid-liquid transition involves structural changes within the first shell, beyond reorganization of the interstitial region and tetrahedral order.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Unraveling hidden Raman modes in ${\alpha}$-MnTe: Effects of long-range dipole-dipole interactions on phonon bands
arXiv_CondMat.summary: In this study, we address the seemingly open question of disparity between the experimentally and theoretically observed Raman spectra for the altermagnetic $\alpha$-MnTe. We establish that the consideration of long range (LR) dipole-dipole interaction is crucial to accurately estimate the phonon band structure and thereby capturing each of the experimentally observed Raman signatures. The LR correction brings about substantial changes to the high-frequency optical modes and their group-theoretical representations. Specifically, for the highly debated Raman peak around 175 cm$^{-1}$, alongside the Raman silent B$_{1u}$ mode, the LR corrections introduce Raman-active longitudinal optical A$^{\prime}$ and A$_1$, and transverse optical A$_1$ modes. Overall, the calculated Raman spectra suggest that the intensity of these modes is weak in the pristine system, while certain prescribed distortions can increase their intensity. The Raman peak around 140 cm$^{-1}$, as observed experimentally, is identified to be emerging from a higher-order Raman process due to zone off-center contributions, while the other debated 120 cm$^{-1}$ peak has both the zone center and off-center contributions.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Efficient Optimization of Tensor Rings with Low-Rank Environments
arXiv_CondMat.summary: Tensor-ring (TR) decompositions provide a natural representation of periodic systems but are difficult to optimize because the closed geometry prevents a global canonical form and leads to costly, ill-conditioned environments. Existing periodic Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) methods alleviate this difficulty by compressing long environments to a low-rank representation, reducing local operations to $\mathcal{O}(p\chi^3)$, where $p$ is the retained environment rank. Here, we extend this approach to an efficient two-site Ring-DMRG algorithm and improve its numerical robustness through appropriate gauge transformations and a generalized Davidson solver. A central challenge in the two-site formulation is the truncation step, which must account for the surrounding environment. When this environment is sufficiently separable, a suitable change of frame reduces the truncation to an ordinary singular value decomposition. When it is not separable, we instead use an alternating optimization that retains the full environment. The computational advantage of tensor rings over tensor trains depends on the scaling of the required environment rank $p$ with bond dimension and system size. For critical systems, the divergent correlation length makes long-range observables remain sensitive to the periodic geometry as the thermodynamic limit is approached. In this regime, the environment rank required to reach a fixed accuracy in the observable does not grow with the system size. Ring-DMRG therefore retains the same cubic scaling with bond dimension as standard DMRG, but at a substantially smaller bond dimension. The low-rank environment construction also provides a systematic generalization of belief propagation (BP), with standard BP recovered in the rank-one limit.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Transport and thermalization under noncommuting localized constraints
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We investigate the effects of spatially localized conserved quantities on transport and thermalization in quantum and classical many-body systems. We consider several related models: the integrable quantum Volterra model, its nonintegrable classical limit, and two cellular automata derived from the latter. Although localized constraints are often associated with lattice gauge theories, our models do not admit such an interpretation. In systems with discrete degrees of freedom, these constraints induce uniform fragmentation of the Hilbert or configuration space. In the quantum Volterra model, we derive an exact mapping of the dynamics within each Hilbert-space fragment onto a quantum chiral Potts chain. We find that energy transport is ballistic, with identical transport coefficients across all fragments. In the nonintegrable classical limit, energy transport is diffusive, and we similarly find the diffusion constant to be independent of whether or not the constraints are fixed (resolved). Finally, in the cellular automata, we show that, despite leaving transport unaffected, localized constraints lead to a strong breakdown of local ergodicity.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Time evolution in the multi-component dynamical Keldysh models
arXiv_CondMat.summary: We construct a time evolution operator for a dynamical quantum models with a multi-component random Gaussian field characterized by a long correlation time. We analyze three paradigmatic cases: non-Abelian $SU(2)$ symmetry class for the three-component Gaussian noise and Abelian symmetry classes $U(1)$ and $Z_2$ for the two- and one-component noises correspondingly. Starting with a limiting case of the infinite correlation time (Keldysh model) we shown that statistics of the two-component random field with a non-zero mean is described by the Rice distribution. We derived and solved the system of coupled linear differential equations for the exact diagonal and off-diagonal single-particle Green's functions. We showed how the finite time correlation in Keldysh models are accounted by a continuous fractions method.

arXiv_CondMat.title: Microscopic structure at the morphotropic phase boundary in lead-barium meta-niobate
